Chrysocolla is Mohs 2.5-3.5 alone but up to 7 locked in chalcedony or quartz, the bead-grade form, from Peru, DR Congo and Arizona. Shattuckite (Mohs about 3.5) was named for Bisbee's Shattuck mine; most now comes from the Kaokoveld, Namibia.
stones.judging: Chrysocolla is robin's-egg to sky blue-green with a waxy to glassy finish; shattuckite is deeper, near-royal blue in fibrous patches, often with black or green. The usual confusion is azurite-malachite, a carbonate: azurite is deep navy, malachite green in concentric bands. Vinegar on a hidden spot fizzes on azurite-malachite, not on the silicates.
stones.name: Chrysocolla and shattuckite
stones.uses: Mid tier. Southwest palettes as a turquoise alternative. Nuggets and ovals sell best.

stones.care: Fades with prolonged heat or sun; store dark; no ultrasonic. Magnesite is soft: earrings and necklaces only.
stones.carried: Smooth round 8mm, rondelle 6 to 9mm, oval 10 to 18mm; tags. At 85 ct per 8 inches of 8mm rounds, cost is ; retail per 8 inch, per 16. The most valuable stone in this tier.
stones.definition: Chalcedony colored apple green by nickel; Mohs 6.5 to 7. Rough from Queensland and Western Australia, Tanzania, Indonesia. "Lemon chrysoprase" is not chrysoprase: it is nickel-bearing magnesite (magnesium carbonate) from Western Australia, Mohs about 3.5 to 4.5.
stones.judging: Even apple green with a translucent glow is the top; grayish and opaque is commercial; brown spots lower it. Lemon magnesite is opaque, light, and a steel point scratches it.
stones.name: Chrysoprase
stones.uses: Fine-jewelry designers and collectors; the high-ticket strand. Rounds and rondelles sell.

stones.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic usually safe. Lemon quartz can fade in prolonged sun.

stones.definition: Yellow to orange-brown quartz, Mohs 7. Natural citrine is uncommon.
stones.judging: Madeira should be saturated orange-brown with no muddy zones; lemon a clean, cool yellow. Look-alikes: glass (bubbles), yellow fluorite (soft).
stones.name: Citrine and lemon quartz
stones.uses: November-birthstone work, autumn palettes, lemon quartz for summer brights. Rondelles and briolettes.

stones.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic fine. Surface-reaching rutile can chip at drill holes.
stones.carried: Faceted pear, rondelle, tube, Herkimer-style nuggets. No tag observed; market wholesale roughly for crystal, for rutilated. Retail: crystal per 16 inches ; rutilated pears per 8, rondelles per 16.
stones.definition: Colorless quartz (rock crystal), Mohs 7; rutilated quartz is rock crystal shot through with golden rutile (titanium dioxide) needles. Rock crystal: Brazil, Madagascar, India; golden rutilated: nearly all Brazilian. "Herkimer diamond" properly means double-terminated quartz from Herkimer County, New York; anything else is "Herkimer-style".
stones.judging: Rutilated: dense, bright gold needles evenly spread; sparse brown needles are lower grade. Look-alikes: glass (round bubbles, swirl marks, warms in the hand; quartz stays cold) and "hydro" synthetic quartz (flawless).
stones.name: Crystal quartz and golden rutilated quartz
stones.uses: Crystal is the universal spacer and "diamond look" filler; rutilated is a neutral with drama. Tubes and pears for earrings; points for pendants.

stones.care: Softer than quartz; no rings, ultrasonic or heat. Water, soft cloth.

stones.definition: White common opal with black tree-like manganese-oxide inclusions; hydrated silica, Mohs 5.5 to 6; rough from Kazakhstan, Turkey, Mexico, Madagascar. "Dendrite opal" is the Indian trade name; "dendritic agate" is the same picture in harder chalcedony (6.5 to 7); "merlinite" is a New Mexico crystal-shop name applied to either.
stones.judging: Crisp black ferns on a clean white ground, one full dendrite per dagger. A steel point scratches opal at the drill-hole edge and skates on agate. Look-alike: printed glass (bubbles; surface pattern only).
stones.name: Dendrite opal
stones.uses: Minimalist and neutral-palette designers, wedding work. Entry to mid tier. Daggers and kites sell best.

stones.care: Warm water, mild soap, soft cloth. No ultrasonic, steam, jewelry dip or hot dashboards.

stones.definition: Green beryl, Be3Al2Si6O18 colored by chromium and vanadium. Mohs 7.5 to 8 but brittle and usually fractured. Bead grades: Zambia, Brazil, lower-grade Colombian and Indian material.
stones.judging: Judge color first: medium green that stays green in daylight, not gray or blackish, shaded evenly. The mossy "jardin" under a loupe confirms beryl.
stones.name: Emerald
stones.uses: Birthstone sellers, makers pairing green with yellow gold, layering designers. Rondelles are volume; hearts and pears are gifts.

stones.care: Remove for showers, swimming and lotion; if it clouds, let it dry a few days. No ultrasonic or heat.
stones.carried: Smooth rondelles 3 to 5mm, rounds, pear drops and nuggets at ; premium bright drops. Opal is light: assume 20 ct per 8 inches at 4mm. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
stones.definition: Hydrated silica, SiO2 with 3 to 10 percent water. Mohs 5.5 to 6.5. Mined in Wollo (Welo) province, Ethiopia, found 2008. Hydrophane: it soaks up water, turns temporarily clear, then dries back.
stones.judging: Buy play-of-color: a good bead flashes green, orange and blue from several angles. Reject crazing (spidery cracks under a loupe). Opalite glass glows milky blue with no real flash; synthetic opal shows a too-regular "lizard skin" pattern. A water drop on Welo soaks in within a minute.
stones.name: Ethiopian Welo opal, white and crystal
stones.origins: Hydrophane: it soaks up water, turns temporarily clear, then dries back
stones.uses: Etsy fine-jewelry makers, October birthstone sellers, boho and bridal designers. Drops for earrings and pendants are the profit item.

stones.care: Mohs 4 in plain terms: a steel pin, a key or house dust (quartz, Mohs 7) will scratch it, and a knock on a table edge can split a bead along a cleavage plane. Earrings and necklaces only; never bracelets or rings. Cool soapy water; no ultrasonic, heat or acids.
stones.carried: Smooth rondelles, faceted tubes and heishi in banded multicolor at. Assume 120 carats per 16 inches of 6-8mm rondelles: retail half for 8 inches.
stones.definition: Calcium fluoride. Mohs 4, perfect cleavage in four directions. Banded "rainbow" bead material comes almost entirely from China.
stones.judging: Saturated bands with sharp color changes and good transparency; gray or mostly colorless beads are the low end. Faceted tubes should have crisp facet junctions; a rushed polish rounds them. Check drill holes for flat or stepped chips, early cleavage.
stones.name: Fluorite
stones.uses: Entry tier. Candy palettes, crystal-shop buyers, gift lines. Rondelles and heishi sell best.

stones.care: Last on, first off. No perfume, acids or ultrasonic. Damp cloth.
stones.carried: Baroque fireball 15 to 25mm and round 8 to 10mm, white with pink or mauve overtone; printed tags read as retail stickers. Assuming 16-inch strands, fireballs retail by luster and tail; rounds. Resale stock, not Jaipur.
stones.definition: Nacre (mostly aragonite with conchiolin) grown by freshwater mussels on Chinese farms; China is the only commercial producer. Mohs 2.5 to 4.5. Rounds are tissue-nucleated solid nacre; "fireball" pearls are bead-nucleated baroques with a round body and flame-shaped tail.
stones.judging: Luster is everything: sharp reflections mean thick nacre, fuzzy means thin. Fireballs want a blemish-light body and metallic tail; rounds want matched size and few pits.
stones.name: Freshwater cultured pearl
stones.uses: Bridal and classic designers, single-fireball pendants, layering necklaces. Mid tier.

stones.care: Fragile. Soft damp cloth only; no ultrasonic, steam or solvents.
stones.carried: Smooth oval, faceted pear, rondelle, heishi; ; 15 SKUs online. Retail: rondelles per 16 inches ; pears and ovals per 8.
stones.definition: and GIA does not recognize the name; the base varies by supplier.
stones.judging: Prove the base. Feldspar shows flat parallel cleavage planes and sheen from inside; glass shows round bubbles and surface-only sheen.
stones.name: Gray silverite
stones.uses: Shimmery gray for evening and bridal work below pearl prices. Faceted pears and rondelles.

stones.care: Both fine for bracelets.

stones.definition: Green aventurine is natural Indian quartzite (Mohs 6.5 to 7) full of fuchsite, a chromium mica that gives the green and a faint glitter (aventurescence).
stones.judging: Green onyx: uniform bottle green, translucent, no color pooled in drill holes. Aventurine: opaque medium green with mica flecks at 10x. Look-alike: glass (bubbles).
stones.name: Green onyx and green aventurine
stones.uses: Onyx: emerald-color statement shapes cheap. Aventurine: budget "lucky green" bracelets, men's malas. Entry tier. Marquise and kites move.

stones.care: Daily wear. Soap and water.

stones.definition: Hessonite is the cinnamon to honey variety of grossular (calcium aluminum silicate), from Sri Lanka, India and Tanzania. Spessartite is manganese aluminum silicate, brighter mandarin orange, from Nigeria, Namibia and Mozambique. Both Mohs 6.5-7.5; mixed parcels sell as "shaded."
stones.judging: Hessonite alone shows a swirled, oily "treacle" look inside under a 10x loupe. Citrine is glassy and clean inside, paler, and a same-size strand weighs about 27 percent less (SG 2.65 against 3.65). Fire opal weighs about half as much, is softer (Mohs 5.5-6.5, a steel point scratches it) and often hazy.
stones.name: Hessonite and spessartite garnet
stones.uses: Mid tier. Autumn palettes and Vedic astrology buyers asking for "gomed" (hessonite). Shaded heishi and 3mm rondelles sell best.

stones.care: Daily wear is fine; avoid hard knocks along the cleavage. Soap and water.
stones.carried: Smooth ovals and faceted heishi at. Assume 150 carats per 16 inches of 8x10mm ovals: retail half for 8 inches. Faceted 4mm heishi, 45 carats: retail.
stones.definition: Gem cordierite, a magnesium-iron aluminum silicate. Mohs 7-7.5, one direction of cleavage. Most bead material is from India; also Tanzania and Sri Lanka. Nicknamed "water sapphire" for its pale sapphire look.
stones.judging: Iolite is strongly pleochroic: violet-blue in one direction, pale blue-gray in another, straw yellow in the third. In an oval bead one face looks inky and the side washed out; good cutters drill so the blue faces out, so check most beads read blue from the front. Look-alikes: tanzanite (far pricier, different pleochroic colors) and blue glass (no pleochroism, bubbles).
stones.name: Iolite
stones.uses: Entry tier. Denim and slate palettes, budget "sapphire look" pieces. Faceted heishi sells best.

stones.care: Necklaces and earrings; feldspar scratches in bracelets. Soapy water; no acids, which attack azurite.
stones.carried: Faceted marquise 25 to 30mm, rectangle 15 to 25mm, pyramid, kite, slices; 12 SKUs online at. Tag not read. At 200 ct per 8 inches of 25mm marquise, retail per 8 inch, per 16.
stones.definition: Not a jasper. White granite (quartz, plagioclase, muscovite, biotite) with round orbs of blue azurite, from the foot of K2 in the Karakoram, Skardu district, Pakistan. Granite is Mohs 6 to 7, azurite 3.5 to 4, but the azurite is a stain along grain boundaries, so the orbs polish like the granite.
stones.judging: Clean white ground with several saturated blue orbs per bead is the top; gray speckled ground with one faint dot the bottom (price the gray lot lower). Orbs should be soft-edged, fading into granite that glitters with mica.
stones.name: K2 granite
stones.uses: Men's and unisex lines, "modern rustic" designers. Mid tier. Marquise, bars and kites sell.

stones.care: Not a beach or windowsill stone; no ultrasonic, steam, hot water, halogen lamps or bracelets.

stones.definition: Pink to lilac spodumene, lithium aluminum silicate, LiAlSi2O6, colored by manganese. Mohs 6.5 to 7 with perfect cleavage in two directions. Bead-grade rough: Afghanistan, Pakistan, Brazil, Madagascar.
stones.judging: Kunzite is pale, so bigger beads show more color; 4mm rondelles look like glass. Turn a bead and it shifts pink, violet and near colorless. Rose quartz is cloudier with no color shift. Reject beads with cleavage planes reaching the drill hole.
stones.name: Kunzite
stones.uses: Bridal and blush-palette designers, statement makers who want big pale beads. Melons as focal runs; tubes for bar pendants.

stones.care: Necklaces and earrings. Bracelets wear the soft direction fast, and a knock along the blade can split a bead; holes drilled across the blade hold better. Soap and water.
stones.carried: Faceted rondelles, ovals, box beads, 9-10mm pears, smooth ovals; blue, teal and multi. Tags. Assume 55 carats per 16 inches of 4mm rondelles: retail. Ovals and boxes, 200 carats: retail ; 8-inch pear strands.
stones.definition: Aluminum silicate that grows as flat blades. Hardness depends on direction: about 4.5-5 along the blade, 6.5-7 across it, hence its old name disthene, "two strengths," plus perfect cleavage in one direction. Blue is mainly Nepalese and Indian; Brazil and East Africa supply teal.
stones.judging: Look for even color and a bright polish on the flat face; Nepal blue is the top color. Teal and green are graded for lack of gray. Box and oval beads are sliced parallel to the blade, showing the soft face; check edges for white flaky spots, early cleavage.
stones.name: Kyanite
stones.uses: Entry to mid tier. Designers who want sapphire blue at a working price. Faceted rondelles and pears sell best.

stones.care: Earrings, pendants and loose necklaces; hard knocks cleave it; big nuggets chip at the edges. Warm soapy water only; no ultrasonic or steam.
stones.carried: Faceted pear, dagger, rectangle, rondelle, coin, flat nugget, statement pieces to 35mm;, tags inverse to size. Retail: rondelles per 16 inches, half for 8; statement strands per 8.
stones.definition: Plagioclase feldspar (sodium calcium aluminum silicate), Mohs 6 to 6.5, perfect cleavage. The flash (labradorescence) is light reflecting off thin twin layers inside a gray to black body. Bead rough is mostly Madagascan.
stones.judging: Blue over most of the bead is standard "AA"; gold, green and purple alongside blue is "AAA" at about double.
stones.name: Labradorite
stones.uses: The gray-with-fire neutral for silver and boho work. Daggers and pears for earrings; nuggets and rectangles for statement necklaces.

stones.care: Pendants and earrings daily, bracelets with care. Mild soap, soft brush; no ultrasonic or solvents.
stones.carried: Faceted 5mm rondelles, daggers, cubes, tubes, smooth rounds, graduated rondelles, denim-grade ovals. Tags. Assume 70 carats per 16 inches of 5mm rondelles: retail half for 8 inches.
stones.definition: A rock, not a mineral: mostly lazurite with pyrite flecks and calcite. Mohs 5-6. Best material: Badakhshan, Afghanistan; Chile supplies most calcite-rich "denim" grade.
stones.judging: Grades: top is deep royal blue with gold pyrite and no visible white; middle has more pyrite and calcite spots; denim is pale with much calcite. an acetone swab picks up blue. Sodalite, the usual substitute, is purplish with white veins and no pyrite.
stones.name: Lapis lazuli
stones.uses: Entry to mid tier. Navy-and-gold palettes, men's bracelets. Faceted 5mm rondelles and 8mm rounds sell best.

stones.care: Necklaces and earrings, careful bracelets. The blue can fade after years of sun; store dark. No ultrasonic or heat.
stones.carried: Faceted pear briolettes, smooth nuggets, ovals and drops at 10-15mm, rondelles. Nuggets ; briolettes. Assume 240 carats per 16 inches of nuggets: retail half for 8 inches. 8-inch briolette strands : retail.
stones.definition: Trade name for blue pectolite, a sodium calcium silicate hydroxide colored by copper. Mohs 4.5-5. One source: Los Chupaderos near Barahona, Dominican Republic.
stones.judging: Top grade is sky to deep "volcanic" blue with white cloud pattern and no gray or green; the pattern follows radiating fibers, not flat patches. A copper coin won't scratch larimar; a steel pin will.
stones.name: Larimar
stones.uses: Upper-mid tier. Beach designers, wire wrappers, collectors of single-source stones. Nuggets and drops sell best; briolettes for earrings.

stones.care: Hard but cleavable: avoid sharp knocks and ultrasonic. Color is stable in sunlight.
stones.carried: Faceted pears, marquise, tubes, carved melons, cubes, tyres and rondelles at. Assume 20 ct per 8 inches at 3mm, 35 at 4mm. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
stones.definition: Topaz, aluminum fluorosilicate, Al2SiO4(F,OH)2. Mohs 8 with one direction of perfect cleavage. "London blue" is a color name (deep steel blue with a green tint), not an origin.
stones.judging: Real London blue is nearly always eye-clean, so judge depth of color (inky teal, not aqua) and facet sharpness. The threat is hydrothermal quartz in the same color, common in tubes. Weigh matching beads: topaz is about a third heavier than quartz.
stones.name: London blue topaz
stones.uses: Fine-jewelry designers wanting saturated blue without sapphire money, December birthstone sellers. Pears and marquise for earrings, melons as focals.

stones.care: Daily-wear durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic usually safe. Strong sun can lighten it.

stones.definition: Pink to peach beryl colored by manganese; same family and chemistry as aquamarine, Mohs 7.5 to 8. Bead rough: Brazil, Mozambique, Nigeria.
stones.judging: Pale by nature; "good" is soft peach-pink with real transparency and glassy luster. The usual confusion is rose quartz: cheaper, cloudier, pinker, and hazy throughout under a loupe, where morganite has clear windows and sharper facets.
stones.name: Morganite
stones.uses: Bridal and blush palettes with rose gold; a step-up from rose quartz. 6mm rondelles and tubes for bracelets.

stones.care: no ultrasonic, chemicals or soaking.
stones.carried: Smooth heishi 4 to 5mm at ; large tyre mixes, tag not read. At 33 ct per 8 inches of heishi, cost is about ; retail per 8 inch, per 16; tyre mixes per 16.
stones.definition: Strands assembled in Jaipur from cutting-room remainders: 4 to 5mm heishi mixing carnelian, chalcedony, chrysoprase, amethyst, moonstone and opal, and large tyre mixes of lapis, amazonite, pink opal and sunstone. Only as tough as the softest bead (opal, Mohs 5.5 to 6).
stones.judging: A good mix has a repeating color plan, even sizing, and no filler. Identify by species, not color.
stones.name: Multi-gemstone heishi and designer mix strands
stones.uses: Beginners and bracelet makers who want a palette on one string, kit sellers. Entry tier, high volume.

stones.care: Necklaces and earrings; brittle edges make it a poor bracelet stone. Warm soapy water, no ultrasonic.
stones.carried: Faceted rondelles 3 to 4mm, pear briolettes and smooth ovals in multi and brown at. Zircon is heavy: assume 26 ct per 8 inches at 3mm, 48 at 4mm. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
stones.definition: Mohs 6 to 7.5, brittle at facet edges, very dense, high fire. Brown and multi zircon comes from Tanzania, Sri Lanka and Madagascar.
stones.judging: Good natural zircon is lively: honey, cognac, red-brown, olive. Under a loupe, facet edges appear doubled, which single-refractive cubic zirconia never shows. Smoky quartz matches the color but is far lighter with no doubling.
stones.name: Natural zircon
stones.uses: December birthstone sellers, designers pairing warm browns with gold, buyers who want fire without diamond prices. 3mm rondelles and briolettes sell best.

stones.care: Earrings and pendants; cleavage makes it chip, so avoid rings. Warm soapy water only; no ultrasonic, steam or sudden heat.
stones.carried: Faceted pear, marquise, rectangle, heishi. Top online sellers: peach 20 SKUs, gray 18. No tag observed; bead-market wholesale roughly. Retail: pears and marquise per 8 inches ; heishi per 16.
stones.definition: The orthoclase moonstones: potassium feldspar with thin albite layers that scatter light into a soft glow. (K,Na)AlSi3O8, Mohs 6 to 6.5, two cleavage directions. Body color from trace iron. Sources: nearly all India.
stones.judging: Clean body color with a visible moving sheen when tilted; flat beads with no glow are low grade. Look-alikes: opalite glass (uniform glow, bubbles), sunstone sold as peach moonstone (sunstone glitters, moonstone glows).
stones.name: Peach, gray, chocolate and golden-shine moonstone
stones.uses: Neutral and earth-tone designers, bridal in peach, minimalist gray for silver work. Pears and marquise for earrings; heishi for bracelets.

stones.care: Fine for necklaces and earrings, bracelets with care. Soap and water only; no ultrasonic, steam or acids.
stones.carried: Faceted 3mm rondelles, ovals, tubes and cubes, pear briolettes. Tags. Assume 30 carats per 16 inches of 3mm rondelles: retail half for 8 inches. Tubes and ovals, about 120 carats per 16 inches: retail. Briolettes, 8-inch strands of 60-80 carats: retail.
stones.definition: Gem olivine (forsterite), a magnesium-iron silicate; iron gives the yellow-green. Mohs 6.5-7, no cleavage but brittle. Bead material is mostly Chinese (Hebei) and Pakistani (Kohistan); Arizona (San Carlos) supplies small sizes.
stones.judging: Pure to slightly yellowish green with no brown; 3mm peridot is never dark. "Lily pad" disc inclusions and tiny black specks are normal and confirm natural origin. Under a loupe peridot shows strong doubling of the far facets; glass doesn't double and shows bubbles. Check drill holes for chipping.
stones.name: Peridot
stones.uses: Mid tier. August birthstone pieces, spring greens with freshwater pearl, olive-and-gold palettes. Faceted rondelles and briolettes sell best.

stones.care: As pink opal: no ultrasonic, chemicals, heat or soaking.
stones.carried: Blue smooth oval 10x14 with dendritic matrix, ; multi rondelles 5 to 7mm,. At 110 ct per 8 inches of ovals and 60 ct of rondelles, blue ovals retail per 8 inch ; multi.
stones.definition: Common opal from the same copper-country deposits as pink opal (Acari, Arequipa); blue-green credited to copper, dendrites to manganese oxide. Mohs 5.5 to 6.5. "Multi Peruvian opal" is mixed pink, blue, green and tan common opal.
stones.judging: Blue: clean sky to teal with sharp dendrites is the top; muddy gray-green with heavy matrix the bottom. Multi should look soft and slightly uneven.
stones.name: Peruvian blue opal and multi Peruvian opal
stones.uses: Blue ovals: focal pendants, upper-mid tier. Multi rondelles: beachy, boho work, entry tier.

stones.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic usually safe. Avoid strong sun.

stones.definition: Two pale amethyst lines. Rose de France is a trade name for pale lilac to lavender amethyst, mainly Brazilian. Pink amethyst is a newer name for pinkish-lavender quartz from Patagonia, Argentina, tinted by hematite inclusions. Both quartz, Mohs 7.
stones.judging: Color is meant to be soft, so judge evenness and clarity: consistent lilac, eye-clean, crisp facets. Pink amethyst shows faint red-brown hematite dusting under a loupe.
stones.name: Pink amethyst and Rose de France
stones.uses: Pastel and bridal palettes with rose quartz, moonstone and pearl. Nuggets for statement necklaces; rondelles as spacers.

stones.care: Earrings and necklaces; bracelets scuff. Porous: no ultrasonic, perfume, soaking or heat.

stones.definition: Common opal (opal-CT with the clay mineral palygorskite), pink from organic compounds, no play-of-color. Mohs 5.5 to 6.5. Rough from Peru, mainly the Acari area of Arequipa.
stones.judging: Even warm pink without gray; cream mottling is normal and cheaper; never glassy. Look-alikes: an acetone swab lifts it).
stones.name: Pink opal
stones.uses: Soft-palette designers: bridal, spring, baby pieces, gold-fill bracelets. Mid tier. Rounds, heishi and tubes sell best.

stones.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic usually safe. No steam or torch nearby.

stones.definition: Green quartz, Mohs 7. natural green quartz (Poland) is not what the bead trade sells.
stones.judging: Pale, clean, slightly yellowish green with good transparency is correct; vivid or bottle-green is suspect. Look-alikes: hydrothermal "hydro" quartz and glass (both too even and clean; glass shows round bubbles), green fluorite (Mohs 4).
stones.name: Prasiolite
stones.uses: Spring palettes and "peridot without the price" designs. Long ovals for stations; melons for statements.

stones.care: Dry box with silica gel; wipe after wear; never shower, swim or sleep in it. Not for rings.

stones.definition: Iron sulfide, FeS2, "fool's gold." Metallic brass-yellow, Mohs 6 to 6.5 but brittle, and heavy (specific gravity about 5, twice chalcedony). It oxidizes slowly in humid air into iron sulfates and traces of sulfuric acid ("pyrite decay"). Rough is mostly Peruvian (Huanzala district) and Chinese.
stones.judging: Even brass color, mirror-bright facets, no dull brown patches (early tarnish), crisp edges, no cracks radiating from drill holes. Real pyrite leaves a greenish-black streak on unglazed tile.
stones.name: Pyrite
stones.uses: Men's bracelets, mixed-metal and industrial styles. Entry to mid tier. Bars, daggers and heishi sell best.

stones.care: Earrings and necklaces, not rough-wear bracelets; hard knocks split it. Warm soapy water only; no ultrasonic or steam.

stones.definition: White labradorite, a plagioclase feldspar (sodium calcium aluminum silicate), not orthoclase moonstone; the blue or multicolor sheen is light scattering off thin internal layers. Mohs 6 to 6.5, perfect cleavage. Bead rough: mostly India.
stones.judging: Strong blue flash across most beads is the top grade; a few blue beads and the rest chalky is the bottom. Look-alike: opalite, a milky glass that glows the same from every angle and shows bubbles; feldspar sheen switches off as you tilt.
stones.name: Rainbow moonstone

stones.definition: Almandine-pyrope garnet, sold as "Mozambique garnet" for its clean red with a faint orange warmth. Iron-magnesium aluminum silicate, Mohs 7-7.5, no cleavage. Mined in Mozambique; Indian and Sri Lankan red garnet gets mixed into parcels.
stones.judging: Pure red to slightly orange-red in daylight, not purple (that's rhodolite) and not so dark the center goes black. Large ovals always read dark, so judge them against a window. Red glass shows bubbles and swirls and weighs about a third less at the same size.
stones.name: Red Mozambique garnet
stones.uses: Entry to mid tier. The workhorse red for holiday pieces and men's 8mm bracelets. Faceted rondelles sell best.

stones.care: Necklaces and earrings only. Perfume, sweat and any acid etch it. Damp cloth and dry; no soaking, ultrasonic or heat.
stones.carried: Smooth banded ovals at 15-20mm,. Assume 290 carats per 16 inches: retail or for 8 inches.
stones.definition: Manganese carbonate. Mohs 3.5-4, perfect cleavage in three directions. Banded pink-and-cream bead material comes from the Capillitas mine, Catamarca, Argentina, where it formed as stalactites in old copper-silver workings, hence "Inca Rose."
stones.judging: Strong rose to raspberry bands alternating with cream or white, sharp and concentric, with translucency at the edges. Pale, mostly cream beads are the low grade. A drop of vinegar at the drill hole fizzes on rhodochrosite and calcite, not agate or rhodonite; rinse at once.
stones.name: Rhodochrosite
stones.uses: Mid tier. Pink palettes, single-focal necklaces. Large ovals show the bands; small rondelles don't.

stones.care: Daily wear. Warm soapy water, soft brush.

stones.definition: Pyrope-almandine garnet, the purplish red to raspberry garnet. Magnesium-iron aluminum silicate, Mohs 7-7.5, no cleavage. Sources: Tanzania, Mozambique, Sri Lanka, India (Odisha), Madagascar.
stones.judging: Even raspberry with a purple flash in daylight and no brown; brick tones mean almandine sold up as rhodolite. Rondelles should be eye-clean and unchipped at the hole. Look-alikes: pink glass (round bubbles, dead-even color) and rubellite tourmaline (pricier; doubles back facets under a loupe, garnet doesn't).
stones.name: Rhodolite garnet
stones.origins: Tanzania, Mozambique, Sri Lanka, India (Odisha), Madagascar

stones.definition: Translucent pink quartz, Mohs 7, colored by microscopic fibers of a pink dumortierite-type mineral, which is why it is always hazy. Sources: Brazil, Madagascar, South Africa, India.
stones.judging: Even medium pink with a soft glow and no gray or brown; chalky white is the low grade. A transparent pink bead at this price is not rose quartz.
stones.name: Rose quartz
stones.uses: Entry-price pink for bracelet stacks, gift lines, bulk stringing. 3 to 4mm rondelles as spacers and full strands.

stones.care: lemon juice, bleach, jewelry dip and a torch etch it. Soft cloth only.

stones.definition: Red corundum, Al2O3 colored by chromium, Mohs 9. Bead grades: India, Mozambique, Madagascar, Myanmar.
stones.judging: Assume glass filling until proven otherwise. and dull glassy patches at the drill hole. Garnet stays dark under UV; ruby glows red.
stones.name: Ruby
stones.uses: Birthstone sellers, budget bridal, red accents in gold fill. 2mm spacers and teardrop earrings sell best.

stones.definition: A metamorphic rock from the Mundarara mine near Longido, Tanzania: green zoisite with opaque red to pink ruby (corundum) and black hornblende. Hardness is mixed, zoisite Mohs 6 to 7, ruby 9, so the ruby stands proud on polished beads.
stones.judging: Buyers want all three colors on every bead: strong green, clear red, some black; mostly green with pink specks is commercial. Facets undercut where soft zoisite meets hard corundum; feel for grooves. Look-alike: ruby-in-fuchsite (softer, sparkly mica).
stones.name: Ruby zoisite
stones.uses: Holiday designers, watermelon-palette fans, men's lines wanting color. Mid tier. Marquise and daggers move fastest.

stones.care: Daily wear, ultrasonic fine. Store apart from softer stones.

stones.definition: Corundum, aluminum oxide (Al2O3); every color but red is sapphire. Mohs 9. Bead grades: Sri Lanka, Madagascar, Tanzania (Umba, Songea), India, cut in Jaipur.
stones.judging: Under a 10x loupe, silk and angular zoning confirm natural corundum; a perfectly clean, uniform strand at $2/ct is glass or synthetic. Glass shows round bubbles; sapphire scratches a quartz bead.
stones.name: Sapphire
stones.uses: Gold-fill fine-jewelry makers, bridal and birthstone sellers. 2 to 3mm rondelles on wire-wrapped chain are the volume item; pink briolettes for earrings.

stones.care: A fingernail can mark it. Earrings and short necklaces worn occasionally; never bracelets. Dry or barely damp cloth; no soaking or chemicals.

stones.definition: Trade name for clinochlore, a chlorite-group magnesium-iron aluminum silicate, in a form with silvery mica-like feathers on dark green. Mohs 2-2.5, among the softest beads sold. One source: the Korshunovskoye iron mine in Irkutsk Oblast, Eastern Siberia.
stones.judging: A strong silver "angel wing" shimmer that moves as you tilt the strand, on deep green rather than gray-green. Check for flaking at drill holes and edges; chlorite is layered and peels. Nothing else has the feather pattern.
stones.name: Seraphinite
stones.uses: Entry to mid tier. Crystal-shop and metaphysical buyers, earring makers. 4mm rondelles and heishi are the whole market; it's too soft for large beads.

stones.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic fine. Strong heat can lighten it.
stones.carried: Smooth rondelle and faceted heishi. No tag observed; bead-market wholesale roughly. Retail: about per 16 inches, half for 8.
stones.definition: Brown quartz, Mohs 7, colored by natural radiation acting on trace aluminum. "Cognac quartz" is a bead-trade name for warm golden-brown smoky quartz, not a separate variety. Sources: Brazil, Madagascar, Colorado.
stones.judging: Clear brown you can read through, even bead to bead. Look-alikes: glass (bubbles), brown obsidian (shell-like chips, no zoning).
stones.name: Smoky and cognac quartz
stones.uses: Neutral, earthy palettes, men's bracelets, autumn lines; a cheap partner for citrine. Smooth rondelles and heishi.

stones.care: Pendants and earrings only. No ultrasonic, steam or bracelets. Store alone in a soft pouch; other beads will scratch it.

stones.definition: Calcium titanium silicate, CaTiSiO5. Mohs 5 to 5.5 with cleavage, so a collector's gem, not a ring stone. Its dispersion (0.051) beats diamond's (0.044), so clean pieces throw real fire. Gem material: Madagascar, Pakistan (Skardu), Sri Lanka, Brazil, Mexico.
stones.judging: Color runs yellow-green, olive and brownish green; greener and more transparent is better. Transparent ovals show fire even polished smooth. Under a loupe, sphene shows very strong doubling and near-adamantine luster. Peridot is the closest color match but is harder, oily-looking and has no fire.
stones.name: Sphene
stones.uses: Collectors, gemologists, designers who want a stone nobody else at the show can name. Ovals as pendant focals.

stones.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic fine. Aventurine is slightly porous; no harsh cleaners.

stones.definition: Two materials, one loose name. Strawberry quartz: translucent quartz with red hematite inclusions (often mislabeled "lepidocrocite"), Mohs 7. Red aventurine: quartzite colored by hematite and mica, faint sparkle, Mohs 6.5 to 7. Sources are inconsistently reported; India supplies most aventurine.
stones.judging: Strawberry quartz: translucent body with visible red flecks or needles. Red aventurine: opaque brick-red with faint glitter. under a loupe, round bubbles and smooth flowing swirls.
stones.name: Strawberry quartz and red aventurine
stones.uses: Pink and red bracelet stacks, Valentine's lines. Heishi and rondelles as spacers; pears for earrings.

stones.care: Earrings and necklaces; cleavage makes it chip. Warm soapy water only; no ultrasonic or steam.

stones.definition: Feldspar with aventurescence, a glittery copper-red sparkle from tiny flat platelets of hematite or copper. Bead-grade sunstone is oligoclase or orthoclase feldspar from Tamil Nadu, India, and Tanzania; Oregon is a different price tier. Mohs 6 to 6.5, two cleavage directions.
stones.judging: Warm orange-red body with a metallic glitter that flashes in patches as you tilt. Look-alike: goldstone, a copper-flecked glass, sparkles uniformly from every angle, shows bubbles, and comes in blue and green; sunstone never does.
stones.name: Sunstone
stones.uses: Warm autumn and southwestern palettes, men's heishi bracelets, a glittering partner for labradorite. Heishi and flat nuggets stand out.

stones.care: Warm soapy water; avoid hard knocks and ultrasonic on drilled beads. Color is stable.

stones.definition: The same topaz, Al2SiO4(F,OH)2, Mohs 8. Sky blue is a pale aquamarine-like blue; Swiss blue is bright electric blue.
stones.judging: Eye-clean is normal, so judge evenness of color and crispness of faceting. Sky blue should have no gray; Swiss no green. so the weight test applies.
stones.name: Swiss blue and sky blue topaz
stones.uses: Volume buyers making affordable "something blue" pieces, birthstone sellers. Coins and nuggets to statement designers; 4mm rondelles to everyone else.

stones.care: Necklaces and earrings, not bracelets or rings. No ultrasonic, steam or sudden temperature change.

stones.definition: Blue-violet zoisite, calcium aluminum silicate, Ca2Al3(SiO4)3(OH). Mohs 6 to 7 with one direction of perfect cleavage. One source on earth: the Merelani Hills near Arusha, Tanzania.
stones.judging: Commercial tanzanite is light lavender to grayish blue, often cloudy; saturated blue-violet with a purple flash is better. Turn a bead: tanzanite shows blue one way and violet or bronze another. Iolite is harder, lighter, grayer, and swings from violet-blue to nearly colorless.
stones.name: Tanzanite

stones.definition: Complex boron silicate; elbaite is the species behind pink, green and watermelon. Mohs 7 to 7.5, no cleavage, strongly pleochroic. Bead grades: Afghanistan, Nigeria, Brazil, Mozambique, Madagascar.
stones.judging: A good multi strand has clean pinks, greens and blues with few muddy brown-olive beads. Tourmaline is darker along the crystal's length than across it, and facet edges double under a loupe. Real watermelon slices show a rounded-triangular outline and a pink core grading to green rind.
stones.name: Tourmaline
stones.uses: Designers wanting color variety, October birthstone sellers, wire-wrappers. Multi rondelles are volume; slices and briolettes are high-ticket focals.

stones.definition: Hydrated copper aluminum phosphate. Mohs 5-6, porous. Bead material comes from Arizona (Kingman still operates; Sleeping Beauty closed in 2012), China (Hubei), Iran and, since 2013, Kazakhstan's Altyn-Tyube deposit (Golden Hills). Mine names can't be lab-confirmed.
